statement: In linear time-invariant (LTI) systems theory and engineering, the continuous-time transfer function H(s) is defined as the ratio of the Laplace transform of the output signal Y(s) = L{y(t)} to the Laplace transform of the input signal X(s) = L{x(t)}, giving H(s) = Y(s) / X(s) = L{y(t)} / L{x(t)} (and for discrete-time systems, as the ratio of z-transforms H(z) = Y(z) / X(z) = Z{y[n]} / Z{x[n]}). The supplied sources do not contain a derivation of the transfer function via the Laplace transform of differential equations (e.g., using the Laplace transform of derivatives); rather, the transfer function is established by definition as the ratio of output to input transforms, or defined directly as H(s) = 1 / p_L(s) for linear differential operators with exponential inputs.

properties.property: In the Laplace domain, the system output is the product of the transfer function and the input: Y(s) = H(s) X(s)
properties.why: follows directly by algebraic rearrangement of the definition H(s) = Y(s) / X(s)

properties.property: For discrete-time systems, the transfer function is defined using the z-transform as H(z) = Y(z) / X(z) = Z{y[n]} / Z{x[n]}
properties.why: discrete-time signals indexed by integers are represented using the z-transform rather than the continuous Laplace transform

properties.property: For a constant-coefficient differential operator L[u] = r(t) with characteristic polynomial p_L, the transfer function operator F[r] = u acts as a right inverse L[F[r]] = r with H(s) = 1 / p_L(s) wherever p_L(s) != 0
properties.why: substituting the trial solution u(t) = H(s)e^{st} for an exponential forcing function r(t) = e^{st} yields L[H(s)e^{st}] = H(s)p_L(s)e^{st} = e^{st}

properties.property: The frequency response and gain under sinusoidal excitation are obtained by evaluating the transfer function on the imaginary axis s = j\omega (setting \sigma = 0), yielding gain G(\omega) = |H(j\omega)| and phase shift \phi(\omega) = arg(H(j\omega))
properties.why: setting the real part \sigma = 0 reduces the bilateral Laplace transform to the Fourier transform for steady-state analysis

properties.property: A transfer function system is strictly stable if and only if all of its poles have strictly negative real parts (\sigma_P < 0)
properties.why: any pole with a positive real part produces a transient response term diverging to infinity as time tends to infinity

properties.property: The frequency-dependent delays introduced by the transfer function are given by phase delay \tau_\phi(\omega) = -\phi(\omega) / \omega and group delay \tau_g(\omega) = -d\phi(\omega) / d\omega
properties.why: phase delay measures the time delay of the carrier sinusoid while group delay measures the derivative of phase shift representing delay to the envelope

assumptions.assumption: The system is linear and time-invariant (LTI)
assumptions.breaks_when: The system has nonlinear characteristics or time-varying internal parameters

assumptions.assumption: The Laplace transform of the input signal X(s) is non-zero and well-defined on the region of convergence
assumptions.breaks_when: The input signal does not have a valid Laplace transform or X(s) = 0

assumptions.assumption: The complex frequency s is not a root of the characteristic polynomial, p_L(s) != 0
assumptions.breaks_when: s coincides with a system pole, causing the denominator to vanish

assumptions.assumption: For steady-state sinusoidal response evaluations H(j\omega), the system is strictly stable and operating in steady state
assumptions.breaks_when: Transient responses do not decay (poles with non-negative real parts) or observation occurs during fleeting turn-on/turn-off transients

failure_modes.mode: System instability and unbounded transient growth
failure_modes.signature: Temporal output g(t) diverges to infinity as t -> \infty
failure_modes.cause: One or more poles of the transfer function H(s) have positive real parts (\sigma_P > 0)

failure_modes.signature: H(s) is undefined / division by zero
failure_modes.cause: Evaluation of H(s) at s = s_P where characteristic polynomial p_L(s) = 0

failure_modes.signature: Output does not follow |H(j\omega)| \sin(\omega t + arg(H(j\omega)))
failure_modes.cause: Presence of non-decaying transient response components or lack of strict stability
